title: NLL 2026-27 Season Preview: Toronto Defends Its Crown Without CJ Kirst as the League Opens November 27 on FloLacrosse
excerpt: The 2026-27 NLL season opens November 27 with defending champion Toronto missing star CJ Kirst to injury, Jeff Teat debuting in Oshawa, new rule changes and every game streaming on the new home of FloLacrosse.
content:
The 2026-27 National Lacrosse League season opens November 27, when the Saskatchewan Rush visit the Oshawa FireWolves, and the defending champions will raise their banner the next night without their brightest young star. The Toronto Rock host the San Diego Seals on November 28 after sweeping Halifax in last season's finals for the franchise's seventh NLL championship.

Toronto opens its title defense without CJ Kirst, the reigning NLL Rookie of the Year. Kirst suffered a lower-body injury during the outdoor season and is expected to miss the start of the campaign, with the Rock expecting him back in the new year but giving no specific return date. The injury also keeps him out of December's Global Lacrosse Games. Kirst is coming off a remarkable year: he led the Philadelphia Waterdogs to the PLL championship on September 20, earning PLL MVP honors with 42 goals and nine assists in 12 games, and posted 34 goals and 37 assists in 18 NLL games.

The other big offseason move belongs to Oshawa, which acquired Jeff Teat first overall in the dispersal draft. Teat is also recovering from an injury, and the FireWolves have not confirmed a return date, leaving the season's most intriguing debut on hold. Buffalo, which had chased a fourth consecutive championship, saw its bid end with a 17-10 quarterfinal loss to Georgia, while Halifax finished 8-10, grabbed the final playoff spot and still reached the NLL Finals.

The league also heads into the season with new rules. An offensive player who steps into the crease can now be the first to receive a pass, provided the player re-establishes position outside the crease before a teammate gains possession, a clarification that followed a controversial overtime winner in last season's playoffs. Coaches now get up to three challenges per game in regulation, officials will only initiate replay review in the final minute of the fourth quarter and in overtime, and the league will experiment with a 20-second shot clock on offensive possession resets during eastern preseason games.

Everything will be easier to watch this season. FloLacrosse officially launched November 5 as the exclusive global streaming home of the NLL under a multiyear partnership, carrying every regular-season and playoff game, and FloSports announced a $25,000 Impact Player of the Month award program. The 12-team league plays 18-game schedules, with San Diego now playing its home games at Frontwave Arena in Oceanside and Rochester rebuilding under two-time championship-winning coach Troy Cordingley with No. 1 draft pick Finn Thomson.

Sources: FloLacrosse; Inside Lacrosse.
